name: max_flow_min_cut
author: da50612d
description: Maximum flow from a source node to a sink node (Edmonds-Karp) and the minimum cut that limits it. Use for questions like 'how much can flow / how many routes or edge-disjoint paths are there from A to B?', 'where is the bottleneck between A and B?', 'which links must be cut to separate A from B?'. Needs 'source' and 'sink' node ids (use lookup_node first). Edge capacity comes from 'capacity': 'weight' (default; on airports this is distance in km), 'unit' (every edge = 1, so the flow counts edge-disjoint paths and the cut is the fewest links to remove), or a numeric edge attribute such as 'airlines' on airports. Works on directed graphs (flow follows edge direction) and undirected graphs (an edge carries flow either way). Returns max_flow_value, the cut edges (largest capacity first, up to top_k, each with from/to node and capacity), the cut size and the sizes of the two sides.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

source.description: Node id where the flow starts (from lookup_node).

sink.description: Node id where the flow ends (from lookup_node); must differ from source.

capacity.description: What limits each edge: 'weight' (edge weight), 'unit' (every edge carries 1), or the name of a numeric edge attribute such as 'airlines'.

top_k.description: How many minimum-cut edges to list.
